QF.id: AIFM CIII Legal Documents and Negotiations_21

question.text: Which of the following statements about SEBI's relationship with the PPM of a Cat III AIF is CORRECT?

answer.text: SEBI approves the PPM as true and accurate before any AIF launches a scheme.
SEBI provides only observations on the PPM; it does not approve the document, and responsibility for accuracy rests with the Manager.
SEBI's observations are confidential and never shared with the merchant banker.
SEBI guarantees the performance claims in the PPM's Track Record section.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9.5 contains SEBI's standard disclaimer: 'submission of the PPM to SEBI should not in any way be deemed or construed that the same has been cleared or approved by SEBI. SEBI does not take any responsibility for the accuracy and correctness of disclosures... It is Manager's responsibility to take all reasonable care...' The Trap: Option A is a common lay misconception — SEBI REGISTRATION is distinct from APPROVAL of PPM contents. Option C wrongly makes observations secret; they're communicated to the merchant banker. Option D is fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same disclaimer. XIX-B tests that distributors must not claim 'SEBI-approved PPM'. XXI-B PMS has a similar 'disclosure, not approval' framework. Manager's Pro-Tip: Paste SEBI's disclaimer verbatim on the PPM cover page AND in all investor pitch decks — it shields the Manager from misrepresentation claims that SEBI 'vetted' the fund.
